movement_source: row 'Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) (APRA Level 2)', column 30 Jun 25 -> column 30 Jun 26
headline: CBA's APRA Level 2 CET1 ratio fell 30bpts to 12.0% at 30 June 2026 from 12.3% at 30 June 2025, still well above APRA's 10.25% minimum (ev-1, ev-44, ev-52). The ratio was squeezed because RWA grew faster than capital: total RWA rose 5% to $522,407m from $496,145m (ev-19, ev-45) while CET1 capital rose only $1,795m to $62,762m (ev-26). Credit risk RWA rose 6% to $422,703m (ev-46) — the bank states it "deployed 72bpts of capital into credit risk weighted assets" across FY26 on volume growth in commercial portfolios and domestic mortgages (ev-53). Offsetting: cash NPAT of $10,982m, up 7% (ev-48), against a $5.05 fully-franked DPS with a 77% payout ratio and a fully-neutralised DRP (ev-47, ev-56). Level 1 CET1 fell 30bpts to 12.1% and the internationally comparable ratio 40bpts to 18.3% (ev-17, ev-18) — context measures only. CBA publishes no FY26-vs-FY25 CET1 walk; only a Dec 25→Jun 26 walk (ev-6).

drivers.bank_label: Credit Risk RWA / capital deployed into credit risk weighted assets
drivers.narrative: CBA states it "deployed 72bpts of capital into credit risk weighted assets with strong volume growth particularly in commercial portfolios and domestic residential mortgages" across FY26. Credit risk RWA rose 6% to $422,703m from $398,928m; AIRB residential mortgage RWA rose to $159,139m from $149,143m, including an $8.2bn Australian Residential Mortgage PD model overlay (Jun 25: a $2.4bn self-imposed risk weight floor).

IRRBB RWA rose to $41,659m from $39,841m (ev-22). CBA's own Jun 26 vs Jun 25 bridge splits this: Jun 25 $40bn, APS 117 -$10bn, underlying movement +$12bn, Jun 26 $42bn (ev-42) — i.e. the revised APS 117 framework, effective 1 October 2025, relieved RWA while underlying hedge settings added more. The bank publishes no bpts CET1 impact for the full year; half-on-half IRRBB cost 16bpts (ev-8). Drivers: "higher swap rates and deposit and equity hedge settings that are calibrated to provide stronger earnings stability through a rate cycle".

The revised APS 117 framework took effect 1 October 2025, inside the FY26 window, and reduced IRRBB RWA by $10bn on a Jun 26 vs Jun 25 basis (ev-42). CBA notes "Jun 25 was based on the APS117 framework in effect prior to 1 October 2025, comprising of repricing & yield curve risk, basis risk and optionality risk" (ev-59). No CET1 bpts impact is disclosed for this change, so it is left unquantified.

Operational risk RWA rose to $51,041m from $47,624m, a $3,417m full-year increase, though it was flat half-on-half (0bpts, ev-10). Under APS 115 it is "determined based on the annual average value of the relevant components of the Group's net income over the financial years ended 30 June 2025, 2024 and 2023" — a mechanical reset off rising income, not a risk-profile change. No bpts CET1 impact is published for the full year.

Traded market risk RWA fell to $7,004m from $9,752m, a $2,748m full-year release that partly cushioned the ratio. Half-on-half it was a $3bn or 30% fall, worth +8bpts of CET1 (ev-9), "primarily driven by the securities financing portfolio" (ev-61). CBA discloses no full-year bpts figure.

Cash NPAT from continuing operations of $10,982m, up 7% on FY25's $10,252m (statutory $10,911m, up 8%), was the principal source of capital, lifting net retained earnings to $46,531m from $43,911m. CBA lists "Capital generated from earnings" first among the drivers of the CET1 change (ev-4). In the half-on-half walk Cash NPAT alone contributed +106bpts (ev-6); no full-year bpts figure is published. Cash NPAT excludes equity-accounted associate profits, which are capital neutral (ev-12).

Dividends absorbed most of the earnings. FY26 DPS was 505c, up 20c or 4% on FY25's 485c, at a 77% cash payout ratio (FY25 79%). The DRP carried "no discount and expected to be fully neutralised": both the 2025 final and 2026 interim DRPs were satisfied by on-market purchase, the interim costing $530m of shares for a -10bpts CET1 impact, so no new shares were issued to replenish capital. The half-on-half walk shows the 1H26 dividend at -76bpts (ev-6); no full-year bpts figure is published.

drivers.bank_label: Other (intangibles, reserves, FX, other regulatory adjustments)
drivers.narrative: CET1 regulatory adjustments were a $1,845m smaller drag at -$16,116m versus -$17,961m, aiding the ratio: the cash flow hedge reserve swung to +$1,364m from -$1,162m and the deferred tax asset deduction fell. Against that, other intangibles deductions rose to -$3,171m from -$2,737m and equity investments to -$4,145m from -$3,260m, while total reserves fell to -$1,428m from +$1,242m. CBA lists "Other regulatory adjustments and movement in reserves" among the drivers (ev-4); the half-on-half bar was -8bpts (ev-6, ev-14). No full-year bpts figure is published.

No contribution. "No buy-back activity was undertaken during FY26" — only $300m of the $1bn on-market buy-back announced 9 August 2023 has ever been completed, and the programme "expires on 12 August 2026 and will not be extended". Shares on issue were unchanged at 1,673,462,358 across FY26, versus 118,000 shares bought back in FY25, so capital returns neither helped nor hurt the ratio this year.

No contribution in FY26. CBA's FY25 walk carried a +20bpts "Divestment" bar for the sale of its remaining interests in Bank of Hangzhou and Vietnam International Commercial Joint Stock Bank; the FY26 walk has no such bar (ev-6). The absence of a repeat is part of why the ratio fell year-on-year, though CBA does not itself frame it that way.

notable_items: No buy-back activity in FY26; only $300m of the $1bn programme ever completed, and it will not be extended (ev-5, ev-55)
Revised APS 117 IRRBB framework effective 1 October 2025, reducing IRRBB RWA by $10bn Jun 26 vs Jun 25 (ev-42, ev-59)
$8.2bn Australian Residential Mortgage PD model RWA overlay at Jun 26 replaces the $2.4bn self-imposed mortgage risk weight floor held at Jun 25 (ev-25)
FY25 benefited from a +20bpts divestment gain (Bank of Hangzhou, VIB) that did not repeat in FY26 (ev-65)
Cash flow hedge reserve regulatory adjustment swung from -$1,162m to +$1,364m, a $2,526m favourable swing inside 'Other' (ev-28)

disagreements.topic: CET1 ratio variant used for the movement
disagreements.explanation: CBA's headline reported measure is the APRA Level 2 (Group) CET1 ratio, printed in the results-book KPI and capital tables (ev-1, ev-44). The Level 1 and internationally comparable ratios are different measures on different perimeters and frameworks; the international ratio's 40bpts fall is quoted as context only (ev-17, ev-18).

disagreements.topic: Walk comparison span available for decomposition
values: Dec 25 -> Jun 26 walk (dividend -76, Cash NPAT +106, RWA -46, Other -8)
disagreements.explanation: Both the results book (p48) and the presentation (p32, p106) publish only a Dec 25 -> Jun 26 CET1 walk, and its own drivers are explicitly labelled "for the 6 months ended 30 June 2026" (ev-4). Its bars therefore cannot be restated as FY26-vs-FY25 contributions. Only the 72bpts credit-RWA deployment (ev-53) is stated on a full-year basis.

The chart's bars sum to -24bpts against a printed -30bpts movement, a 6bpt gap. CBA footnotes that "Due to rounding, numbers presented in this section may not sum precisely to the totals provided" (ev-6 chart page). The printed endpoint of 12.0% governs.

limitations: CBA publishes NO FY26-vs-FY25 CET1 walk. Both the results book (p48) and the presentation (p32, p106) show only the Dec 25 -> Jun 26 half-on-half walk, whose own driver list is explicitly scoped 'for the 6 months ended 30 June 2026'. Its bars (-76 dividend, +106 Cash NPAT, -46 RWA, -8 Other) are reported inside narratives as context for that half only, never as FY-on-FY contributions.

Only one driver is quantified on the task comparison: the 72bpts of capital deployed into credit RWA (ev-53). All other drivers carry contribution null, so the quantified drivers do not sum to the -30bpts movement; the residual of +42bpts is the unquantified net of earnings, dividends, other RWA lines and regulatory adjustments and must not be attributed to any one driver.

The 72bpts credit-RWA figure appears only in the ASX/media release, the weakest of the FY26 sources under the hierarchy. It is directionally corroborated by the results-book credit RWA table (+6% to $422,703m, ev-46, ev-20) but no results-book page restates it in bpts, so it is capped below 90.

Full-year bpts impacts are not disclosed for dividends net of DRP, cash NPAT, IRRBB, operational risk, traded market risk or Other. Where I state $m movements for these I computed them by subtracting the 30 Jun 25 column from the 30 Jun 26 column of the appendix tables; the framing is mine, not CBA's, and no bps conversion is asserted.

The APS 117 relief of -$10bn is disclosed in RWA dollars only, not in CET1 bpts, and its Jun 25 base is on the pre-1 October 2025 framework (ev-59), so Jun 25 and Jun 26 IRRBB RWA are not measured on a like-for-like basis.

The RWA bar in CBA's walk excludes FX, which is carried inside 'Other' along with intangibles, associate profits/losses and reserve movements (ev-13, ev-14). The RWA and Other drivers are therefore not cleanly separable, and Cash NPAT excludes equity-accounted associate results as capital neutral (ev-12).

Operational risk RWA is flat half-on-half but up $3,417m year-on-year purely through the APS 115 three-year net-income averaging reset; CBA states no CET1 bpts cost for this, so the driver is unquantified.

The divestments driver is recorded as a zero contribution because the FY26 walk publishes no divestment bar. This is my inference from the bar's absence plus the FY25 walk's +20bpts bar, not a statement CBA makes about FY26.
Capped at 80: capital_returns +0 bps. The records these claims cite do not state those numbers, so each one is arithmetic over the evidence rather than a figure read from it.
